definition_en: something kept hidden | hidden
example1_en: Please keep the plan a secret until Friday.
example1_zh: 请把计划保密到周五。
example2_en: A secret about a leaking school roof helps nobody; the town needs to know.
example2_zh: 对漏雨校舍屋顶保密谁也帮不了；城镇需要知道。
collocations: keep a secret｜保密 ; in secret｜秘密地
tip_zh: secret 作形容词是“秘密的”。

meanings_zh: v. 上升；起身 | n. 上升；增加
definition_en: to go up, or to stand up | an increase
example1_en: Prices rise when the harvest is poor.
example1_zh: 收成不好时价格上涨。
example2_en: Rivers rise quickly in this valley, so the school keeps boots by the back door.
example2_zh: 这条山谷里河水涨得快，所以学校在后门放着靴子。
collocations: rise by｜上升了 ; give rise to｜引起
tip_zh: rise 是不及物动词。及物的“举起、提高”用 raise。过去式 rose，过去分词 risen。

definition_en: a polite title for a man
example1_en: Yes, sir, I will bring the form tomorrow.
example1_zh: 是的，先生，我明天把表格带来。
example2_en: A letter that begins with Sir still fails if the request itself is unclear.
example2_zh: 以 Sir 开头的信，如果请求本身不清楚，仍然会失败。
collocations: Dear Sir｜敬启者
tip_zh: sir 单独称呼时不大写也可，但在书信 Dear Sir 中要大写。

definition_en: a room where people do written work
example1_en: The teacher is in the office now.
example1_zh: 老师现在在办公室。
example2_en: An office that stays lit all night wastes power and tells the street that nobody switched it off.
example2_zh: 整夜亮灯的办公室既费电，也向街道表明没人去关灯。
collocations: post office｜邮局 ; office building｜办公楼
tip_zh: in the office 表示在办公室里。

definition_en: a person you know and like
example1_en: My friend lent me her notes.
example1_zh: 朋友把笔记借给了我。
example2_en: A friend who checks a rumour before sharing it protects the whole class from a false story.
example2_zh: 先核对谣言再转发的朋友，能保护全班不受假消息影响。
collocations: make friends｜交朋友 ; a friend of mine｜我的一个朋友
tip_zh: make friends with sb 表示与某人交朋友。

meanings_zh: n. 风 | v. 缠绕；蜿蜒
definition_en: moving air | to turn or twist something around
example1_en: The wind closed the classroom door.
example1_zh: 风把门带上了。
example2_en: A strong wind along a river path can make a bike ride to school unsafe.
example2_zh: 河边路上的大风，会让骑车上学变得不安全。
collocations: strong wind｜大风
tip_zh: 作“风”时读 /wɪnd/。作“缠绕”时读 /waɪnd/，过去式是 wound。

definition_en: certain, or reliable
example1_en: Are you sure this is your bag?
example1_zh: 你确定这是你的包吗？
example2_en: Leaders should not be sure a policy works until they have asked the people who live with it.
example2_zh: 领导者在询问真正生活在政策之下的人之前，不应确信政策有效。
collocations: make sure｜确保 ; be sure to｜一定要 ; for sure｜确实
tip_zh: be sure to do 提醒某人一定要做；make sure 后面常接 that 从句。

definition_en: a set of printed pages | to arrange to have something later
example1_en: I borrowed a book from the school library.
example1_zh: 我从学校图书馆借了一本书。
example2_en: A town that closes its bookshop loses a place where people discover titles a screen did not suggest.
example2_zh: 关掉书店的城镇，失去了一个人们发现屏幕不曾推荐的书的地方。
collocations: bookshop｜书店 ; bookmark｜书签
tip_zh: book 作动词是“预订”：book a ticket。

definition_en: not public
example1_en: This is a private letter.
example1_zh: 这是一封私人信件。
example2_en: Private buses may fill a gap, but they often skip the stops that make the least money.
example2_zh: 私人公交也许能补上缺口，但它们常常跳过最不赚钱的站点。
collocations: in private｜私下 ; private school｜私立学校
tip_zh: private 与 public 相对。

definition_en: the place where one lives
example1_en: I left my keys at home.
example1_zh: 我把钥匙落在家里了。
example2_en: A city that offers only expensive flats cannot call itself a home for the nurses and drivers it needs.
example2_zh: 一座只提供昂贵公寓的城市，无法成为它所需的护士和司机的家。
collocations: at home｜在家 ; go home｜回家 ; feel at home｜感觉自在
tip_zh: home 前通常不加 to：go home，不是 go to home。

definition_en: money paid to a government
example1_en: The town uses tax money to repair the bridge.
example1_zh: 城镇用税款修桥。
example2_en: A small tax on plastic bags can change what people carry home from the market.
example2_zh: 对塑料袋征收一小笔税，可以改变人们从市场拎回家的东西。
collocations: income tax｜所得税 ; pay tax｜纳税
tip_zh: tax 作动词是“征税”。

meanings_zh: n. 日期；约会 | v. 注明日期
definition_en: a day of the month, or a planned meeting | to write the day on something
example1_en: Write the date at the top of the page.
example1_zh: 把日期写在页首。
example2_en: The date on a food label matters when a family cannot afford to throw good food away.
example2_zh: 当一个家庭扔不起还好的食物时，食品标签上的日期就很重要。
collocations: out of date｜过时 ; up to date｜最新的
tip_zh: date 作动词是“注明日期”或“约会”。

definition_en: a group of people who meet for an activity
example1_en: I joined the reading club this term.
example1_zh: 这学期我加入了读书社团。
example2_en: A school club that costs money to join leaves out students who cannot pay.
example2_zh: 需要交钱才能加入的学校社团，会把付不起钱的学生排除在外。
collocations: join a club｜加入社团 ; football club｜足球俱乐部
tip_zh: club 也可指棍棒，考纲里更常见的是社团。

definition_en: a feeling, a meaning, or a way of noticing
example1_en: There is a sense of quiet in the library.
example1_zh: 图书馆里有一种安静的感觉。
example2_en: A sense of fairness grows when students see that rules apply to everyone.
example2_zh: 当学生看到规则适用于所有人时，公平感会增长。
collocations: make sense｜讲得通 ; in a sense｜在某种意义上 ; sense of humour｜幽默感
tip_zh: make sense 表示说得通，主语是事物。

definition_en: the reflexive form of I
example1_en: I made the poster myself.
example1_zh: 海报是我自己做的。
example2_en: I asked myself whether a shorter shower would matter if the whole building still wasted water.
example2_zh: 我问自己，如果整栋楼仍在浪费水，缩短淋浴是否还有意义。
collocations: by myself｜独自
tip_zh: myself 作宾语或同位语，不能替代 I 作主语。

definition_en: before now, or sooner than expected
example1_en: I have already handed in the form.
example1_zh: 我已经交了表格。
example2_en: By the time a warning is issued, the river may already have risen over the path to school.
example2_zh: 等到警报发出时，河水可能已经漫过上学的小路。
collocations: already finished｜已经完成
tip_zh: already 多用于肯定句；否定和疑问里表示“尚未”常用 yet。

definition_en: to cover a wider area, or to open something out
example1_en: Open windows so the smell does not spread.
example1_zh: 打开窗户，免得气味扩散。
example2_en: Rumours spread faster than corrections, which is why the first notice must be accurate.
example2_zh: 谣言比更正传得快，所以第一则通知必须准确。
collocations: spread out｜散开 ; spread to｜传到
tip_zh: spread 的过去式和过去分词仍是 spread。

definition_en: a view, or the place where something happens
example1_en: The first scene of the play is a classroom.
example1_zh: 剧的第一场是一间教室。
example2_en: The scene after a flood is not only mud; it is also the question of who will repair the road.
example2_zh: 洪水之后的场面不只是泥，还有谁来修路的问题。
collocations: behind the scenes｜在幕后 ; on the scene｜在现场
tip_zh: scene 可指戏剧的一场、景色或事件现场。

definition_en: a piece of music with words
example1_en: We learned a new song in music class.
example1_zh: 音乐课上我们学了一首新歌。
example2_en: A local song can keep a dialect alive when children no longer hear it at home.
example2_zh: 当孩子在家里不再听到一种方言时，一首本地歌曲能让它继续活着。
collocations: pop song｜流行歌曲 ; sing a song｜唱歌
tip_zh: song 是可数名词。

definition_en: a section of a school, shop, or government
example1_en: She works in the English department.
example1_zh: 她在英语系工作。
example2_en: A health department that shares data with schools can warn them before a heatwave arrives.
example2_zh: 与学校共享数据的卫生部门，可以在热浪到来前发出警告。
collocations: department store｜百货商店
tip_zh: department 是组织里的部门或大学的系。

definition_en: an upright side of a room or a barrier
example1_en: The notice is on the wall.
example1_zh: 通知在墙上。
example2_en: A high wall around a school can keep children safe and also hide the street they need to learn.
example2_zh: 学校周围的高墙可以保护孩子，也会挡住他们需要认识的街道。
collocations: on the wall｜在墙上 ; wall of｜一堵……的墙
tip_zh: 在墙上用 on the wall。

definition_en: a weapon that shoots
example1_en: The museum does not allow a gun in the building.
example1_zh: 博物馆不允许把枪带进楼里。
example2_en: A history lesson about a gun should also ask who was harmed, not only how the machine worked.
example2_zh: 关于枪的历史课也应该问谁受到了伤害，而不只是机器如何工作。
collocations: gun control｜枪支管制
tip_zh: gun 是可数名词。

meanings_zh: v. 在意；关心 | n. 小心；照料
definition_en: to feel that something is important | attention or looking after someone
example1_en: She cares about every student in the class.
example1_zh: 她关心班上的每一个学生。
example2_en: People care more about a park when they helped plant the trees than when they only walk past it.
example2_zh: 人们如果参与种过树，会比只是路过时更在意一座公园。
collocations: care about｜关心 ; care for｜照顾；喜欢 ; take care｜当心
tip_zh: care for 可以是照顾，也可以是“喜欢”，要看语境。

definition_en: the larger part of a group
example1_en: The majority of students walk or cycle.
example1_zh: 大多数学生步行或骑车。
example2_en: A majority vote can still be unfair if the people most affected were not in the room.
example2_zh: 如果受影响最大的人不在房间里，多数票仍然可能不公平。
collocations: the majority of｜大多数
tip_zh: the majority of 加复数名词时谓语常用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 担心 | n. 烦恼；担忧
definition_en: to feel anxious about something | a problem that makes you anxious
example1_en: Do not worry about the result tonight.
example1_zh: 今晚先别为结果担心。
example2_en: Parents worry when the last bus is cancelled and the school has not sent a message.
example2_zh: 末班车取消而学校又没发消息时，家长会担心。
collocations: worry about｜为……担心
tip_zh: worry 后接 about。形容词 worried 形容人，worrying 形容事情。

definition_en: a large boat
example1_en: The ship left the port at dawn.
example1_zh: 船在黎明离开了港口。
example2_en: Goods on a ship still need a road at the other end if a village is to receive them.
example2_zh: 如果一个村子要收到货物，船上的货在另一头仍然需要一条路。
collocations: by ship｜乘船
tip_zh: ship 作动词是“运送”。

definition_en: an adult female person
example1_en: A woman from the clinic spoke to our class.
example1_zh: 诊所的一位女士给我们班讲了话。
example2_en: A woman who works a night shift still needs a safe way home when the last bus has gone.
example2_zh: 上夜班的妇女在末班车走后，仍然需要一条安全的回家路。
collocations: women's day｜妇女节
tip_zh: woman 的复数是 women，读音也变。

meanings_zh: adj. 下一个的；接下来的
definition_en: coming immediately after
example1_en: The next bus leaves in ten minutes.
example1_zh: 下一班车十分钟后开。
example2_en: The next step after collecting data is to ask whether the sample left anyone out.
example2_zh: 收集数据之后的下一步，是追问样本是否漏掉了什么人。
collocations: next to｜在……旁边 ; next week｜下周
tip_zh: next week 前不加 the；the next week 常指过去某个时间之后的一周。

definition_en: a medicine, or an illegal substance
example1_en: The drug must stay in the school clinic.
example1_zh: 这种药必须放在校医务室。
example2_en: Health class should say clearly that a drug from a doctor is not the same thing as an illegal drug.
example2_zh: 健康课应当讲清楚：医生开的药和非法毒品不是一回事。
collocations: drug store｜药店 ; illegal drug｜毒品
tip_zh: drug 既可以是正规药物，也可以是毒品。写作时要加修饰语，避免含糊。

definition_en: the organisation that keeps public order
example1_en: The police helped the children cross the road.
example1_zh: 警察帮助孩子们过马路。
example2_en: Police cannot be the only answer to a dark street; lights and pavements matter too.
example2_zh: 警察不能是黑暗街道的唯一答案；灯和人行道也很重要。
collocations: police station｜警察局 ; police officer｜警官
tip_zh: police 是集体名词，谓语常用复数。一个警察用 a police officer。

definition_en: not old
example1_en: The young trees need water every evening.
example1_zh: 这些小树每天晚上需要浇水。
example2_en: Young workers leave a town when the only jobs are far away and poorly paid.
example2_zh: 当仅有的工作又远又报酬低时，年轻工人会离开城镇。
collocations: young people｜年轻人 ; the young｜年轻人
tip_zh: the young 表示年轻人这一类，谓语用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 数；计算 | n. 计数
definition_en: to say numbers in order, or to be important | an act of counting
example1_en: Count the chairs before the parents arrive.
example1_zh: 家长到之前先数椅子。
example2_en: Every voice should count when a class decides how to share one practice room.
example2_zh: 班级决定如何共用一间练习室时，每个声音都应当算数。
collocations: count on｜依靠 ; count as｜算作
tip_zh: count on somebody 表示依靠某人。count 也可作名词“计数”。

definition_en: the facts of a particular time
example1_en: The situation is better than last week.
example1_zh: 情况比上周好。
example2_en: The situation on a flooded street is not the same as the situation on a dry planning map.
example2_zh: 积水街道上的情况，和干燥的规划地图上的情况不一样。
collocations: in a situation｜处于某种情况
tip_zh: situation 是可数名词。

definition_en: a picture made by a camera
example1_en: She took a photo of the old bridge.
example1_zh: 她给旧桥拍了张照片。
example2_en: A photo of a clean park can hide the street where the rubbish was taken.
example2_zh: 一张干净公园的照片，可以藏起垃圾被运去的那条街。
collocations: take a photo｜拍照
tip_zh: photo 是 photograph 的简写，复数是 photos。

definition_en: every person
example1_en: Everybody in our class joined the clean-up.
example1_zh: 我们班每个人都参加了打扫。
example2_en: Everybody needs a seat at the meeting if the decision will change their bus home.
example2_zh: 如果决定会改变他们回家的公交，每个人都需要在会上有一个座位。
collocations: everybody else｜其他所有人
tip_zh: everybody 后接单数动词。和 everyone 同义，本库两条都保留。不要写成 every body（每一具身体）。

definition_en: to keep doing something
example1_en: Please continue reading after the break.
example1_zh: 休息后请继续阅读。
example2_en: If factories continue to pour waste at night, daytime clean-ups will not save the river.
example2_zh: 如果工厂继续在夜里排污，白天的清理也救不了这条河。
collocations: continue to do｜继续做 ; continue doing｜继续做
tip_zh: continue 后接 to do 或 doing 都可以。

meanings_zh: n. 比赛；火柴 | v. 匹配；比得上
definition_en: a sports game, or a small stick for making fire | to fit or be equal to
example1_en: The football match is on Saturday.
example1_zh: 足球赛在周六。
example2_en: A cup match brings visitors, but the town still needs bins and buses after the final whistle.
example2_zh: 杯赛带来观众，但终场哨响后城镇仍需要垃圾桶和公交。
collocations: match point｜赛点 ; a box of matches｜一盒火柴
tip_zh: match 作动词是“匹配”。win a match，不说 win sb。

definition_en: the organ that pumps blood, or the centre
example1_en: Regular walks are good for the heart.
example1_zh: 经常走路对心脏有好处。
example2_en: A market in the heart of a town keeps daily life there; a mall on the edge can empty the centre.
example2_zh: 镇中心的市场维持着那里的日常生活；边缘的商场可能掏空中心。
collocations: heart disease｜心脏病 ; learn by heart｜记住 ; lose heart｜丧失勇气
tip_zh: by heart 表示靠记忆，不是“靠心脏”。

definition_en: before now
example1_en: The museum closed two years ago.
example1_zh: 博物馆两年前关门了。
example2_en: A factory that shut ten years ago can still leave chemicals in the soil beside a school.
example2_zh: 十年前关闭的工厂，仍可能把化学物质留在学校旁边的土壤里。
collocations: long ago｜很久以前 ; a moment ago｜刚才
tip_zh: ago 用于过去时，放在时间段后面：three days ago。不与现在完成时连用。

meanings_zh: adj. 圆的 | prep. 围绕 | n. 一轮
definition_en: shaped like a circle | around | one stage of an event
example1_en: They sat at a round table.
example1_zh: 他们坐在圆桌旁。
example2_en: A round of talks about the river should include the farms upstream, not only the city.
example2_zh: 关于这条河的一轮会谈应该包括上游的农场，而不只是城市。
collocations: all the year round｜一年到头 ; round trip｜往返行程
tip_zh: 英式里 round 常作介词“围绕”；美式多用 around。

definition_en: a male child
example1_en: Her son walks to school with a neighbour.
example1_zh: 她儿子和邻居一起走路上学。
example2_en: A son who leaves for the city may still send money home, but the village loses his daily help.
example2_zh: 去城市的儿子也许仍会寄钱回家，但村子失去了他日常的帮忙。
collocations: son and daughter｜子女
tip_zh: son 的复数是 sons。

meanings_zh: n. 性格；角色 | n. 角色；人物 | n. 字符；文字
definition_en: personality; a person in a story | a person represented in a story, play, or film | a written or printed symbol, such as a letter
example1_en: Honesty is part of his character.
example1_zh: 诚实是他性格的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving historic buildings helps cities retain their distinctive character while adapting to modern economic demands.
example2_zh: 保护历史建筑有助于城市在适应现代经济需求的同时，保留自身的独特风貌。
collocations: main character｜主要角色 ; strength of character｜坚强品格 ; distinctive character｜独特风貌 ; Chinese characters｜汉字
tip_zh: 作“人物、字符”可数；作整体品质常不可数。

definition_en: to get something that is given or sent
example1_en: I received your message this morning.
example1_zh: 我今天早上收到了你的信息。
example2_en: Students who receive help early are less likely to hide a problem until the exam.
example2_zh: 早点得到帮助的学生，不太会把问题藏到考试。
collocations: receive a letter｜收到信
tip_zh: 拼写是 receive：c 后面是 ei。收到并不等于接受，接受用 accept。

definition_en: perhaps
example1_en: Maybe we can meet after the club.
example1_zh: 也许我们可以在社团活动后见面。
example2_en: Maybe a later school start would help, but only if buses change their times too.
example2_zh: 也许推迟上学时间会有帮助，但只有公交也改时间才行。
collocations: maybe so｜也许如此
tip_zh: maybe 是一个副词；may be 是情态动词加动词，要分开写。

meanings_zh: n. 分数；记号 | v. 做标记；打分
definition_en: a point given for work, or a sign | to write a sign, or to give a score
example1_en: She got a high mark in the reading test.
example1_zh: 她阅读测验得了高分。
example2_en: A single mark on one test should not decide whether a student can join the science club.
example2_zh: 一次测验的一个分数，不该决定学生能否参加科学社团。
collocations: full marks｜满分 ; mark on｜在……上的记号
tip_zh: mark 作动词是“做标记”或“打分”。

meanings_zh: n. 价值 | v. 重视
definition_en: the worth or importance of something | to think something is important
example1_en: The old map still has value for the history class.
example1_zh: 这张旧地图对历史课仍有价值。
example2_en: The value of a library is not only the books, but the quiet hour it gives after school.
example2_zh: 图书馆的价值不只是书，还有它在放学后提供的安静一小时。
collocations: of value｜有价值的 ; value of｜……的价值
tip_zh: value 作动词是“重视”或“估价”。

definition_en: a formal talk, or the power of speaking
example1_en: Her speech at the ceremony was three minutes.
example1_zh: 她在典礼上的演讲只有三分钟。
example2_en: A speech that names no fact can still sound confident, which is why the class checks sources.
example2_zh: 一篇不提事实的演讲仍可能听起来自信，所以班级要核来源。
collocations: make a speech｜发表演讲 ; freedom of speech｜言论自由
tip_zh: speech 表示一次演讲时可数。表示说话能力时不可数。

definition_en: a large area of water surrounded by land
example1_en: We are not allowed to swim in the lake.
example1_zh: 我们不准在湖里游泳。
example2_en: A clean lake supports birds and a town's drinking water at the same time.
example2_zh: 干净的湖同时养活鸟类和一座城镇的饮用水。
collocations: by the lake｜在湖边
tip_zh: lake 是被陆地包围的湖。sea 是海。

meanings_zh: n. 标准 | adj. 标准的
definition_en: a level used for judging | usual or accepted
example1_en: The school raised its safety standard.
example1_zh: 学校提高了安全标准。
example2_en: A national standard for school buses helps only if villages can afford to meet it.
example2_zh: 校车的国家标准只有在乡村负担得起时才有帮助。
collocations: standard of living｜生活水平 ; up to standard｜达到标准
tip_zh: standard 作形容词是“标准的”。

definition_en: to or at a distance
example1_en: She put the phone away during dinner.
example1_zh: 晚饭时她把手机收起来了。
example2_en: Moving factories away from rivers can protect drinking water for the towns downstream.
example2_zh: 把工厂迁离河流，可以保护下游城镇的饮用水。
collocations: far away｜遥远 ; right away｜立刻 ; give away｜赠送；泄露
tip_zh: away 是副词，不单独接宾语；表示离开某地用 away from。

definition_en: inside a limit of time, distance, or area
example1_en: Please reply within three days.
example1_zh: 请在三天内回复。
example2_en: A clinic within walking distance saves families the cost of a long bus ride.
example2_zh: 步行能到的诊所，能为家庭省下长途公交的费用。
collocations: within reach｜在够得着的范围内
tip_zh: within 强调不超过某个范围；in 更一般。

meanings_zh: v. 触摸；接触 | n. 接触；触觉
definition_en: to put a hand on something | an act of touching, or the sense
example1_en: Do not touch the wet paint on the door.
example1_zh: 别碰门上还没干的油漆。
example2_en: A museum that lets students touch a copy of an old tool teaches more than a glass case alone.
example2_zh: 让学生触摸一件古工具复制品的博物馆，比只有玻璃柜教得更多。
collocations: keep in touch｜保持联系 ; touch on｜提及
tip_zh: keep in touch 表示保持联系，不是身体接触。

definition_en: the writer of a book or article
example1_en: The author of the article is a local teacher.
example1_zh: 这篇文章的作者是一位本地老师。
example2_en: An author who hides their name makes it harder to judge the facts.
example2_zh: 隐瞒姓名的作者让人更难判断事实。
collocations: author of｜……的作者
tip_zh: author 是可数名词。

definition_en: a country, or a people
example1_en: The nation celebrates this day in October.
example1_zh: 这个国家在十月庆祝这一天。
example2_en: A nation that funds rural schools changes who gets to sit a university exam.
example2_zh: 资助乡村学校的国家，会改变谁有机会参加大学考试。
collocations: the whole nation｜全国 ; nation-wide｜全国范围的
tip_zh: nation 强调人民或政治共同体。country 更常指国土。

definition_en: a device for speaking to someone at a distance
example1_en: I left my phone in the classroom.
example1_zh: 我把电话落在教室了。
example2_en: A phone warning about a storm helps only the people who still have power and a signal.
example2_zh: 关于风暴的手机警报，只帮助那些还有电和信号的人。
collocations: on the phone｜在打电话 ; phone number｜电话号码
tip_zh: phone 作动词是“打电话”：phone sb。

definition_en: to fail to catch, or to feel sad someone is away
example1_en: I missed the early bus this morning.
example1_zh: 今天早上我错过了早班车。
example2_en: Students miss more than a lesson when a flood closes the only road to school.
example2_zh: 当洪水封了唯一的上学路，学生错过的不只是一节课。
collocations: miss doing｜错过做 ; miss sb｜想念某人
tip_zh: Miss 大写是对未婚女性的称呼，和动词 miss 不同。

definition_en: to send something through the air with the hand
example1_en: Do not throw bags on the stairs.
example1_zh: 不要把包扔在楼梯上。
example2_en: Players who throw the ball too hard in a small hall break both windows and the game.
example2_zh: 在小礼堂里扔球太用力的人，既会打碎窗户，也会毁掉比赛。
collocations: throw away｜扔掉
tip_zh: throw 的过去式是 threw，过去分词是 thrown。

meanings_zh: v. 旅行；行进 | n. 旅行
definition_en: to go from one place to another | the activity of travelling
example1_en: We travel to school by bus.
example1_zh: 我们乘公交去上学。
example2_en: Waste can travel downstream farther than the factory that produced it.
example2_zh: 废物可以向下游流到比产生它的工厂更远的地方。
collocations: travel to｜去……旅行 ; travel by｜乘……旅行
tip_zh: travel 作名词“旅行”通常不可数。

definition_en: to come after, or to obey
example1_en: Follow the signs to the hall.
example1_zh: 按指示牌去大厅。
example2_en: Students follow a timetable, but the buses they need may follow a different one.
example2_zh: 学生遵守课表，但他们需要的公交可能遵守另一份时刻表。
collocations: follow sb｜跟随 ; as follows｜如下
tip_zh: follow 是及物动词，后面直接接宾语，通常不加 to。

definition_en: to make something clear
example1_en: Can you explain this sentence in English?
example1_zh: 你能用英语解释这个句子吗？
example2_en: Charts that explain a water shortage help a town argue for repairs before the next dry summer.
example2_zh: 解释缺水的图表，能帮助一座城镇在下一个干旱的夏天之前争取维修。
collocations: explain sth to sb｜向某人解释
tip_zh: 说 explain something to somebody，不说 explain somebody something。

definition_en: a shiny grey-white metal
example1_en: The medal is silver, not gold.
example1_zh: 这块奖牌是银的，不是金的。
example2_en: A silver cup in a cabinet teaches less than the practice that won it.
example2_zh: 柜子里的银杯，比赢得它的那次练习教得少。
collocations: silver medal｜银牌
tip_zh: silver 也可作形容词“银色的”。

meanings_zh: n. 数字；人物 | n. 人物；人影；身形 | v. 认为；估计
definition_en: a number; an important person | a person, their outline, or the shape of their body | to think or decide something after considering it
example1_en: The figure on the board is wrong.
example1_zh: 黑板上的数字错了。
example2_en: Recent employment figures suggest that investment in public transport can create substantial opportunities for local workers.
example2_zh: 近期就业数据显示，投资公共交通能为当地劳动者创造大量机会。
collocations: sales figures｜销售数据 ; a leading figure｜领军人物 ; figure out｜弄清楚 ; a rough figure｜大致数值
tip_zh: 数据常用复数figures；figure out意为弄懂。

meanings_zh: adj. 商业的 | n. 商业广告
definition_en: related to business and profit | an advertisement on television
example1_en: The commercial street is busy on Sundays.
example1_zh: 商业街周日很忙。
example2_en: Commercial pressure can make a news site publish before the facts are checked.
example2_zh: 商业压力会让新闻网站在事实核对之前就发表。
collocations: commercial centre｜商业中心
tip_zh: commercial 是形容词；commerce 是名词“商业”。

definition_en: a person with authority in an organisation
example1_en: A police officer helped the children cross.
example1_zh: 一位警官帮助孩子们过马路。
example2_en: An officer who explains a rule in plain words is more useful than a sign nobody reads.
example2_zh: 用浅显的话解释规则的官员，比没人读的牌子更有用。
collocations: police officer｜警官 ; army officer｜军官
tip_zh: officer 是人；office 是办公室。

definition_en: to succeed in doing something
example1_en: He worked hard to achieve his goals.
example1_zh: 他努力工作以实现目标。
example2_en: Governments can achieve significant reductions in air pollution by investing in clean energy and improving public transport.
example2_zh: 政府可以通过投资清洁能源和改善公共交通，大幅减少空气污染。
collocations: achieve success｜取得成功 ; achieve a goal｜实现目标 ; achieve a balance｜达到平衡 ; achieve results｜取得成果
tip_zh: 直接接目标或成果，不说achieve to do。

definition_en: the condition of the air at a particular time
example1_en: The weather turned cold after lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭后天气变冷了。
example2_en: Bad weather is a poor excuse for cancelling sport if the hall is empty and safe.
example2_zh: 如果礼堂空着而且安全，坏天气就不是取消体育课的好理由。
collocations: weather forecast｜天气预报 ; in all weathers｜无论什么天气
tip_zh: weather 不可数，不说 a weather。表里这一行的音标是 wear，本库不用。

definition_en: two times
example1_en: I have read the notice twice.
example1_zh: 这则通知我读了两遍。
example2_en: Checking a source twice is cheaper than correcting a story the whole school has already shared.
example2_zh: 把来源核对两遍，比纠正全校已经转发的故事代价更小。
collocations: twice a week｜每周两次 ; twice as big｜两倍大
tip_zh: 次数用 once、twice，三次起用 three times。

meanings_zh: n. 习俗；习惯 | adj. 定制的 | n. 惠顾；光顾
definition_en: a usual practice | made to meet a particular customer's needs | the business customers give to a shop or company
example1_en: Shaking hands is a common custom.
example1_zh: 握手是一种常见习俗。
example2_en: Schools can introduce children to local customs while encouraging respect for traditions from other cultures.
example2_zh: 学校可以向孩子们介绍当地风俗，同时鼓励他们尊重其他文化的传统。
collocations: local customs｜当地风俗 ; an ancient custom｜古老的习俗 ; custom furniture｜定制家具 ; regular custom｜经常光顾
tip_zh: custom指风俗或惯例；customs还可指海关。

definition_en: to become or make larger
example1_en: The number of bikes increased this term.
example1_zh: 这学期自行车的数量增加了。
example2_en: If rents increase faster than wages, workers move farther from the jobs a city needs.
example2_zh: 如果房租涨得比工资快，工人会搬得离城市需要的工作更远。
collocations: increase by｜增加了 ; increase to｜增加到
tip_zh: increase 作名词时重音常在前，作动词时重音常在后。

definition_en: very nearly
example1_en: I almost missed the early bus.
example1_zh: 我差点错过早班车。
example2_en: A plan that is almost finished still fails if the last step, such as a safe crossing, is missing.
example2_zh: 一个几乎完成的计划，如果缺了最后一步，比如安全的过街处，仍然会失败。
collocations: almost all｜几乎全部 ; almost never｜几乎从不
tip_zh: almost 可修饰 all、every、no；nearly 一般不修饰 no 和 never 的否定极限，习惯上用 almost no。

definition_en: a place of higher education
example1_en: She hopes to study biology at university.
example1_zh: 她希望在大学学生物。
example2_en: A university that ignores the town around it will not see the housing problems its students face.
example2_zh: 忽视周围城镇的大学，看不到自己学生面对的住房问题。
collocations: go to university｜上大学 ; university student｜大学生
tip_zh: go to university 泛指上大学，常不加 the。

definition_en: one or the other of two
example1_en: You may take either seat.
example1_zh: 两个座位你坐哪个都行。
example2_en: Either the bus comes on time or students start arriving late, and then the first lesson suffers.
example2_zh: 要么公交准时，要么学生开始迟到，然后第一节课受影响。
collocations: either...or｜要么……要么 ; not...either｜也不
tip_zh: either...or 连接主语时，谓语与靠近的主语一致。否定句末的“也”用 either，不用 too。

definition_en: to hand something to someone, or to provide
example1_en: Please give the form to your class teacher.
example1_zh: 请把表格交给班主任。
example2_en: Cities that give buses their own lanes often move more people than cities that only widen roads.
example2_zh: 给公交车专用车道的城市，往往比只拓宽马路的城市运送更多人。
collocations: give up｜放弃 ; give out｜分发 ; give sb a hand｜帮忙
tip_zh: give sb sth 或 give sth to sb，两种语序都可以。

definition_en: a group chosen to decide or organise something
example1_en: The committee will meet on Friday.
example1_zh: 委员会周五开会。
example2_en: A committee that never visits the street may approve a road the residents do not want.
example2_zh: 从不走那条街的委员会，可能会批准居民不想要的路。
collocations: a member of the committee｜委员会成员
tip_zh: committee 作整体时谓语可用单数。

meanings_zh: n. 营地；营 | v. 野营
definition_en: a place where people stay in tents or simple buildings | to stay in a tent
example1_en: The summer camp lasts five days.
example1_zh: 夏令营为期五天。
example2_en: A camp near a river needs a night plan for rain, not only a list of games.
example2_zh: 河边的营地需要夜里下雨的方案，而不只是一份游戏清单。
collocations: summer camp｜夏令营 ; camp out｜野营
tip_zh: camp 作动词是野营。

definition_en: a substance like air, or fuel
example1_en: The science class learned about natural gas.
example1_zh: 科学课学习了天然气。
example2_en: A gas leak near a school is an emergency, not a smell to ignore until tomorrow.
example2_zh: 学校附近的煤气泄漏是紧急情况，不是可以拖到明天的气味。
collocations: natural gas｜天然气 ; gas station｜加油站
tip_zh: 美式 gas 常指汽油；英式汽油多用 petrol。

definition_en: connected with religion
example1_en: The museum has a room of religious art.
example1_zh: 博物馆有一间宗教艺术展室。
example2_en: A public school can teach religious history without telling students which faith to follow.
example2_zh: 公立学校可以教宗教史，而不必告诉学生该追随哪种信仰。
collocations: religious belief｜宗教信仰
tip_zh: religious 是形容词。宗教本身是 religion。

meanings_zh: n. 力量；武力 | v. 强迫
definition_en: strength, or a group organised to use power | to make someone do something
example1_en: The wind had enough force to shut the door.
example1_zh: 风力大得把门关上了。
example2_en: A city should not use force as the first answer to a peaceful student march.
example2_zh: 一座城市不该把武力当作对学生和平游行的第一反应。
collocations: by force｜用武力 ; labour force｜劳动力
tip_zh: force sb to do 表示强迫某人做。

definition_en: used to agree or accept
example1_en: Yes, I can stay after class to help.
example1_zh: 是的，我可以课后留下来帮忙。
example2_en: A quick yes from a committee means little if nobody records who will do the work.
example2_zh: 委员会随口答应没什么用，如果没人记下谁来干活。
collocations: yes or no｜是或否
tip_zh: yes 用来肯定；对否定疑问句回答要按事实，而不是顺着问句。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……后面 | adv. 在后面
definition_en: at the back of | at the back
example1_en: The lab is behind the library.
example1_zh: 实验室在图书馆后面。
example2_en: The reasons behind a high absence rate may be buses and jobs, not only a lack of interest.
example2_zh: 高缺勤率背后的原因可能是公交和工作，而不只是缺乏兴趣。
collocations: fall behind｜落后 ; behind time｜迟到
tip_zh: behind 是介词或副词。落后用 fall behind。

meanings_zh: adj. 伟大的；极好的；巨大的
definition_en: very good, important, or large
example1_en: We had a great time at the school fair.
example1_zh: 我们在校园义卖上玩得很开心。
example2_en: A great increase in visitors can damage the very places people travel to see.
example2_zh: 游客的大量增加，可能破坏人们专程去看的那些地方。
collocations: a great deal of｜大量 ; greatly｜非常
tip_zh: a great many 后接可数名词复数。

definition_en: the reflexive form of he
example1_en: He fixed the bike himself.
example1_zh: 他自己修好了自行车。
example2_en: A mayor who walks the flooded street himself learns more than one who only reads a report.
example2_zh: 亲自走过积水街道的市长，比只读报告的市长了解得更多。
collocations: by himself｜独自
tip_zh: himself 不能代替 he 作主语。

definition_en: a television station, a narrow sea, or a way through
example1_en: We changed the channel to hear the news.
example1_zh: 我们换了频道听新闻。
example2_en: The English Channel is one channel; a student hotline is another kind of channel.
example2_zh: 英吉利海峡是一种 channel，学生热线是另一种渠道。
collocations: change the channel｜换频道 ; the English Channel｜英吉利海峡
tip_zh: channel 可以是电视频道、海峡或沟通渠道。

meanings_zh: adj. 自己的 | v. 拥有
definition_en: belonging to the person mentioned | to possess
example1_en: I wrote the speech in my own words.
example1_zh: 我用自己的话写了这篇演讲。
example2_en: A town that grows its own vegetables is less shaken when outside supplies are delayed.
example2_zh: 自己种菜的城镇，在外部供应延误时受到的冲击更小。
collocations: on one's own｜独自 ; of one's own｜属于自己的
tip_zh: own 前要有物主代词：my own，不能单独说 own book。

definition_en: the two together
example1_en: Both answers are possible.
example1_zh: 两个答案都有可能。
example2_en: A city needs both affordable housing and good schools if it wants families to stay.
example2_zh: 如果一座城市希望家庭留下来，就既需要付得起的住房，也需要好学校。
collocations: both...and｜既……又 ; both of｜两者都
tip_zh: both...and... 连接并列成分，谓语用复数。

definition_en: medical surgery, or the way something works
example1_en: The operation was successful.
example1_zh: 手术成功了。
example2_en: The operation of a night bus depends on drivers, fuel, and a timetable people trust.
example2_zh: 夜班公交的运转取决于司机、燃料，以及人们信任的时刻表。
collocations: in operation｜在运转 ; have an operation｜做手术
tip_zh: operation 可指手术或运转，要看语境。

meanings_zh: v. 信任 | n. 信任
definition_en: to believe someone is honest or reliable | belief that someone is reliable
example1_en: I trust her to lock the lab.
example1_zh: 我信任她会锁好实验室。
example2_en: People trust a clinic more when the same nurse is there every week.
example2_zh: 当同一位护士每周都在时，人们更信任一家诊所。
collocations: trust in｜信任 ; trust sb to do｜相信某人会做
tip_zh: trust 后可接 sb to do。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……里面 | adv. 在里面
definition_en: in the inner part of | in the inner part
example1_en: Please wait inside the hall.
example1_zh: 请在大厅里面等。
example2_en: Noise from inside a factory can be lower than the noise of trucks waiting outside it.
example2_zh: 工厂内部的噪音，可能低于在外面等候的卡车的噪音。
collocations: inside out｜里朝外
tip_zh: inside 可作介词或副词。

definition_en: needed
example1_en: A pencil is necessary for the drawing test.
example1_zh: 绘画测验必须带铅笔。
example2_en: It is necessary to tell students why a rule exists, not only what they must not do.
example2_zh: 有必要告诉学生一条规则为什么存在，而不只是不准做什么。
collocations: if necessary｜如果有必要 ; necessary for｜对……是必要的
tip_zh: 常用 It is necessary to do，不说 somebody is necessary to do。

meanings_zh: v. 投票 | n. 选票；投票
definition_en: to choose officially | a choice made in an election
example1_en: The class will vote for a monitor.
example1_zh: 班级将投票选班长。
example2_en: People vote more calmly when the polling place is near and the rules are posted in plain words.
example2_zh: 当投票点很近、规则用浅显的话贴出来时，人们投票会更从容。
collocations: vote for｜投票赞成 ; vote on｜就……投票
tip_zh: vote 作名词是“选票”或“投票”。

definition_en: a journey, often a short one
example1_en: Our class trip is to the history museum.
example1_zh: 我们班的旅行是去历史博物馆。
example2_en: A school trip teaches more when students write what they saw, not only where they went.
example2_zh: 如果学生写下看到了什么，而不只是去了哪里，学校旅行就教得更多。
collocations: a day trip｜一日游 ; business trip｜出差
tip_zh: trip 常指较短或有目的的出行。动词 trip 是绊倒。

meanings_zh: adj. 慷慨的 | adj. 充足的；大量的
definition_en: willing to give | larger or more plentiful than usual or expected
example1_en: She is generous with her time.
example1_zh: 她在时间上很大方。
example2_en: Generous donations from local businesses can help community centres provide affordable activities for children and older residents.
example2_zh: 当地企业的慷慨捐助可以帮助社区中心为儿童和老年居民提供价格实惠的活动。
collocations: generous donation｜慷慨捐助 ; generous portion｜丰盛的一份 ; generous with your time｜不吝惜时间
tip_zh: be generous with sth表示在某方面慷慨。

definition_en: a piece of furniture for sleeping
example1_en: I went to bed at ten.
example1_zh: 我十点上床睡觉。
example2_en: A student who goes to bed after midnight will feel the cost in the first lesson.
example2_zh: 午夜后才上床的学生，会在第一节课感受到代价。
collocations: go to bed｜上床睡觉 ; in bed｜在床上
tip_zh: go to bed 指去睡觉；sleep 是睡觉这个动作。

definition_en: television
example1_en: We watched the news on TV.
example1_zh: 我们在电视上看了新闻。
example2_en: TV can warn a town about a storm, but only if people still have electricity.
example2_zh: 电视可以警告城镇有风暴，但前提是人们还有电。
collocations: on TV｜在电视上 ; TV set｜电视机
tip_zh: TV 是 television 的缩写，前面常用 on。

definition_en: not different
example1_en: We took the same bus home.
example1_zh: 我们乘了同一班车回家。
example2_en: Two schools can follow the same timetable and still offer very different support to struggling students.
example2_zh: 两所学校可以执行同样的课表，但对学习吃力的学生提供的帮助仍然很不一样。
collocations: the same as｜和……一样 ; at the same time｜同时
tip_zh: same 前面通常加 the。

definition_en: to think something will happen
example1_en: I expect the bus at eight.
example1_zh: 我预计公交八点到。
example2_en: Parents expect a safe walk to school, not only a high score at the end of the year.
example2_zh: 家长期待的是安全的上学路，而不只是年底的高分。
collocations: expect to do｜预计做 ; expect sb to do｜期望某人做
tip_zh: expect 后接 to do 或 sb to do，不接 doing。

meanings_zh: n. 气氛；大气 | n. 大气；大气层
definition_en: the feeling of a place; air around Earth | the mixture of gases surrounding a planet
example1_en: The classroom had a friendly atmosphere.
example1_zh: 教室里气氛友好。
example2_en: A supportive classroom atmosphere encourages students to ask questions and participate more actively in discussions.
example2_zh: 相互支持的课堂氛围鼓励学生提问，并更加积极地参与讨论。
collocations: relaxed atmosphere｜轻松的氛围 ; create an atmosphere｜营造氛围 ; Earth's atmosphere｜地球大气层
tip_zh: 表示某种氛围常用an atmosphere；地球大气用the atmosphere。

definition_en: a recording of moving pictures
example1_en: We watched a short video about the river.
example1_zh: 我们看了一段关于这条河的短视频。
example2_en: A video can spread a false claim widely before anyone has time to check the pictures.
example2_zh: 一段视频可以在任何人来得及核对画面之前，把一个虚假说法传得很广。
collocations: video clip｜视频片段 ; make a video｜拍视频
tip_zh: video 可数。看视频用 watch a video。

definition_en: throughout a period of time
example1_en: Please do not talk during the exam.
example1_zh: 考试期间请不要说话。
example2_en: During a drought, schools can show families how small daily changes save a surprising amount of water.
example2_zh: 干旱期间，学校可以向家庭展示，日常的小改变能省下惊人的水量。
collocations: during the day｜在白天 ; during the holiday｜在假期期间
tip_zh: during 后接名词，不接句子；接句子用 while 或 when。

meanings_zh: adj. 谦虚的；适度的 | adj. 适度的；不大的 | adj. 穿着端庄的
definition_en: not boastful; not large | not large in size, amount, or cost | wearing clothes that do not reveal much of the body
example1_en: She is modest about her success.
example1_zh: 她对自己的成功很谦虚。
example2_en: Even a modest increase in public transport funding could improve services in rural communities.
example2_zh: 即使公共交通拨款只小幅增加，也可能改善农村社区的服务。
collocations: modest about one's achievements｜对自己的成就谦虚 ; a modest increase｜小幅增长 ; a modest income｜不高的收入
tip_zh: 形容人常指谦虚；形容数量常指不大。

meanings_zh: n. 证据 | v. 表明；证明
definition_en: facts that prove something | To show clearly that something exists or is true.
example1_en: There is no evidence of cheating.
example1_zh: 没有作弊的证据。
example2_en: Governments should consider scientific evidence before introducing policies intended to improve public health outcomes.
example2_zh: 政府在推出旨在改善公共健康状况的政策前，应考虑科学证据。
collocations: strong evidence｜有力证据 ; scientific evidence｜科学证据 ; evidence of｜……的证据 ; provide evidence｜提供证据
tip_zh: 作名词通常不可数：一项证据用a piece of evidence。

meanings_zh: n. 方法；靠近 | v. 接近；靠近 | v. 着手处理；接洽
definition_en: a way of dealing with something | To move nearer to someone or something. | To begin dealing with something or contact someone about it.
example1_en: A new approach may solve the problem.
example1_zh: 新方法可能解决这个问题。
example2_en: A balanced approach to urban planning should consider both economic growth and the protection of green spaces.
example2_zh: 均衡的城市规划方法应兼顾经济增长和绿地保护。
collocations: an approach to learning｜学习方法 ; adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; approach a problem｜着手处理问题 ; approach someone for advice｜找某人征求建议
tip_zh: 名词“方法”后用to加名词或动名词；动词后直接接宾语。

meanings_zh: adj. 道德的 | n. 寓意；教训
definition_en: about right and wrong | a lesson about right and wrong learned from a story
example1_en: The story has a moral lesson.
example1_zh: 这个故事有道德寓意。
example2_en: Companies have a moral responsibility to ensure that their suppliers provide safe working conditions.
example2_zh: 企业在道义上有责任确保其供应商提供安全的工作环境。
collocations: moral responsibility｜道德责任 ; moral dilemma｜道德困境 ; moral support｜精神支持 ; the moral of the story｜故事的寓意
tip_zh: moral指道德；morale指士气，注意拼写区别。

meanings_zh: v. 进行；指挥 | v. 传导热或电 | n. 行为；举止
definition_en: to carry out; to lead | to allow heat or electricity to pass through | the way a person behaves, especially towards others
example1_en: Scientists conduct experiments in the lab.
example1_zh: 科学家在实验室进行实验。
example2_en: Researchers should conduct thorough trials before recommending new treatments for widespread use in public hospitals.
example2_zh: 研究人员在建议公立医院广泛采用新疗法之前，应开展充分的试验。
collocations: conduct research｜开展研究 ; conduct a survey｜进行调查 ; conduct electricity｜导电 ; code of conduct｜行为准则
tip_zh: 动词重音在后；名词重音在前，英音/ˈkɒndʌkt/。

meanings_zh: v. 辩论 | v. 辩论；讨论 | v. 仔细考虑；权衡
definition_en: to discuss opposing views | To discuss a subject by considering different views. | To think carefully about options before making a decision.
example1_en: Students will debate the topic in class.
example1_zh: 学生们将在课堂上辩论这个话题。
example2_en: The debate over free public transport centres on its environmental benefits and the cost to taxpayers.
example2_zh: 关于免费公共交通的争论集中在其环境效益和纳税人需要承担的费用上。
collocations: public debate｜公开讨论 ; heated debate｜激烈的辩论 ; debate an issue｜讨论一个问题 ; debate whether to｜斟酌是否要
tip_zh: 动词可直接接议题；debate whether to表示权衡。

definition_en: helpful
example1_en: Walking is beneficial to health.
example1_zh: 散步有益健康。
example2_en: Access to green spaces is particularly beneficial to urban residents who have limited opportunities for outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 对于户外锻炼机会有限的城市居民来说，能够使用绿地尤其有益。
collocations: beneficial effect｜有益影响 ; beneficial to health｜有益健康 ; mutually beneficial｜互利的
tip_zh: 常接to或for，说明对谁或哪方面有益。

meanings_zh: n. 边界；界限 | n. 界限；限度
definition_en: a line that marks a limit | A limit defining acceptable behaviour or the scope of something
example1_en: Respect personal boundary at work.
example1_zh: 在工作中尊重个人界限。
example2_en: Clear boundaries between work and personal life can protect employees' mental health and reduce long-term stress.
example2_zh: 明确工作与个人生活的界限，可以保护员工的心理健康并减轻长期压力。
collocations: a national boundary｜国界 ; set boundaries｜设定界限 ; cross a boundary｜越过边界 ; push the boundaries｜突破界限
tip_zh: boundary 强调分界；border 常用于国家或地区边界。

meanings_zh: v. 试图；尝试 | v. 尝试；试图
definition_en: to try | To try to do something, especially something difficult.
example1_en: She will attempt to climb the mountain.
example1_zh: 她将尝试爬山。
example2_en: Many cities are attempting to reduce air pollution by improving public transport and expanding cycling networks.
example2_zh: 许多城市正通过改善公共交通和扩展自行车道网络来尝试减少空气污染。
collocations: make an attempt｜作出尝试 ; attempt to do something｜尝试做某事 ; a successful attempt｜成功的尝试 ; in an attempt to｜为了尝试
tip_zh: 动词后接to do；名词常用an attempt at doing。

meanings_zh: adj. 焦虑的；渴望的 | adj. 渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried; eager | Very eager to do something or for something to happen.
example1_en: She felt anxious before the test.
example1_zh: 考试前她感到焦虑。
example2_en: Students may become anxious about their future when career guidance is unavailable at school.
example2_zh: 学校不提供职业指导时，学生可能会对未来感到焦虑。
collocations: anxious about｜对……感到焦虑 ; anxious to please｜急于讨好 ; feel anxious｜感到焦虑
tip_zh: anxious about表担忧；anxious to do常表急切。

definition_en: to give time or energy to
example1_en: She will devote more time to study.
example1_zh: 她将把更多时间用于学习。
example2_en: Governments should devote more resources to preventive healthcare rather than relying entirely on expensive medical treatments.
example2_zh: 政府应将更多资源投入预防性医疗，而不是完全依赖昂贵的医学治疗。
collocations: devote time to｜投入时间于 ; devote resources to｜投入资源于 ; devote oneself to｜致力于
tip_zh: devote…to中的to是介词，后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 适应；改编 | v. 改编；改装
definition_en: to change to fit a new situation | to change something for a different use or audience
example1_en: Animals must adapt to climate change.
example1_zh: 动物必须适应气候变化。
example2_en: Schools must adapt their teaching methods to meet the needs of students from diverse cultural backgrounds.
example2_zh: 学校必须调整教学方法，以满足不同文化背景学生的需求。
collocations: adapt to change｜适应变化 ; adapt teaching methods｜调整教学方法 ; adapt a novel for television｜把小说改编成电视剧
tip_zh: adapt to后接名词或动名词；勿混adopt（采用）。

meanings_zh: adj. 以前的 | adj. 前者的
definition_en: previous | being the first of two people or things just mentioned
example1_en: He is a former student of this school.
example1_zh: 他是这所学校以前的学生。
example2_en: Former industrial sites can be transformed into public parks, improving urban environments and creating shared spaces.
example2_zh: 昔日的工业用地可以改建为公园，从而改善城市环境并创造共享空间。
collocations: former colleague｜以前的同事 ; former president｜前任总统 ; former industrial site｜昔日工业用地
tip_zh: the former 指两者中的前者，the latter 指后者。

definition_en: easy to see or understand
example1_en: It is evident that she studied hard.
example1_zh: 很明显她学习很努力。
example2_en: The benefits of improved public transport are evident in cities where traffic congestion has decreased.
example2_zh: 在交通拥堵有所缓解的城市，改善公共交通的益处显而易见。
collocations: clearly evident｜十分明显的 ; become evident｜变得明显 ; evident from｜从……可明显看出
tip_zh: 常用It is evident that...表示显然……。

definition_en: enough
example1_en: Food supply is adequate.
example1_zh: 食物供应是足够的。
example2_en: Schools need adequate funding to maintain safe buildings and provide effective support for students with additional needs.
example2_zh: 学校需要充足的资金来保障校舍安全，并为有额外需求的学生提供有效支持。
collocations: adequate funding｜充足的资金 ; adequate preparation｜充分准备 ; adequate for the task｜足以胜任任务
tip_zh: 表示达到所需标准，不等于优秀；常接for或to。

definition_en: real
example1_en: The actual cost was higher.
example1_zh: 实际费用更高。
example2_en: Governments should measure the actual impact of transport policies rather than relying solely on predicted benefits.
example2_zh: 政府应衡量交通政策的实际影响，而不是仅仅依赖预期收益。
collocations: actual cost｜实际成本 ; actual results｜实际结果 ; actual size｜实际大小
tip_zh: actual指实际的，不等于表示目前的current。

meanings_zh: adj. 明显的；表面上的 | adj. 表面上的；看似的
definition_en: easy to see; seeming | Seeming to be true, though possibly not actually true.
example1_en: It was apparent that he was tired.
example1_zh: 很明显他累了。
example2_en: Despite the apparent benefits of remote learning, some students struggle without direct support from teachers.
example2_zh: 尽管远程学习看似有诸多好处，一些学生在缺乏教师直接帮助时仍感到吃力。
collocations: become apparent｜变得明显 ; for no apparent reason｜无明显原因 ; apparent contradiction｜表面上的矛盾
tip_zh: 可指“明显的”，也可指“看似的”，须看语境。

meanings_zh: adj. 逐渐的 | adj. 坡度平缓的
definition_en: happening slowly | Rising or falling gently rather than steeply
example1_en: Progress is often gradual.
example1_zh: 进步往往是逐渐的。
example2_en: A gradual transition to renewable energy can help communities adapt without causing sudden job losses.
example2_zh: 逐步转向可再生能源有助于社区适应变化，避免就业岗位骤减。
collocations: gradual improvement｜逐步改善 ; gradual change｜渐进的变化 ; a gradual slope｜平缓的斜坡
tip_zh: 强调变化缓慢、分阶段；副词形式为gradually。

meanings_zh: v. 假定；承担 | v. 承担；就任 | v. 呈现；具有
definition_en: to suppose; to take on | To take on a duty, responsibility, or position. | To begin to have a particular appearance or quality.
example1_en: Don't assume that everyone knows the rules.
example1_zh: 不要假定人人都知道规则。
example2_en: Policymakers should not assume that all households have reliable internet access or adequate digital skills.
example2_zh: 政策制定者不应假定所有家庭都有稳定的网络连接或足够的数字技能。
collocations: assume that｜假定…… ; assume responsibility｜承担责任 ; assume office｜就任
tip_zh: assume常接that从句，强调未经证实便认为。

meanings_zh: v. 采用；收养 | v. 收养 | v. 正式通过；采纳
definition_en: to take up; to take as one's own | To legally take someone else's child into your family. | To formally approve a proposal, policy, or rule.
example1_en: The school will adopt a new teaching method.
example1_zh: 学校将采用一种新的教学方法。
example2_en: Governments should adopt long-term strategies that improve public transport rather than simply building more roads.
example2_zh: 政府应采取改善公共交通的长期策略，而不是一味增建道路。
collocations: adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; adopt a policy｜采纳一项政策 ; adopt a child｜收养孩子 ; adopt a resolution｜通过决议
tip_zh: adopt是采用或收养；adapt是适应或改编。

meanings_zh: n. 权威；当局 | n. 当局；主管机构 | n. 权威人士；专家
definition_en: power to make decisions | an official body responsible for a particular area or service | a person with extensive knowledge of a particular subject
example1_en: The school authority made a new rule.
example1_zh: 学校当局制定了新规则。
example2_en: Local authorities should consult residents before introducing policies that significantly affect access to public services.
example2_zh: 地方当局在推出显著影响公共服务获取的政策前，应征求居民意见。
collocations: have authority to do something｜有权做某事 ; local authorities｜地方当局 ; an authority on｜某方面的权威 ; abuse of authority｜滥用职权
tip_zh: 表权力通常不可数；the authorities常指当局。

meanings_zh: n. 贡献 | n. 捐款；捐赠物 | n. 投稿；稿件
definition_en: something given to help | Money or goods given to support a person or cause. | A piece of writing supplied for a publication.
example1_en: His contribution to science was huge.
example1_zh: 他对科学的贡献巨大。
example2_en: Public libraries make a valuable contribution to lifelong learning by providing free access to information.
example2_zh: 公共图书馆通过免费提供信息资源，为终身学习作出了宝贵贡献。
collocations: make a contribution to｜为…作出贡献 ; a significant contribution｜重大贡献 ; a voluntary contribution｜自愿捐款
tip_zh: 常用make a contribution to；to后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 欣赏；感激 | v. 欣赏；赏识 | v. 理解；意识到
definition_en: to value or be thankful for | Recognise and enjoy the value or quality of something. | Understand the importance or difficulty of a situation.
example1_en: I really appreciate your help.
example1_zh: 我真心感激你的帮助。
example2_en: Policymakers need to appreciate the difficulties rural communities face when accessing healthcare and other essential services.
example2_zh: 政策制定者需要理解农村社区在获取医疗及其他基本服务时面临的困难。
collocations: greatly appreciate｜非常感激 ; appreciate your help｜感谢你的帮助 ; appreciate the importance of｜认识到……的重要性 ; appreciate art｜欣赏艺术
tip_zh: 可接名词或动名词，不接to do；感谢帮助用appreciate your help。

meanings_zh: adj. 准确的 | adj. 精准的；命中目标的
definition_en: correct and exact | able to hit or reach the intended target
example1_en: Give an accurate answer, please.
example1_zh: 请给出准确答案。
example2_en: Accurate information about air quality enables residents to make informed decisions about outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 准确的空气质量信息能帮助居民在充分知情的情况下决定是否进行户外锻炼。
collocations: accurate information｜准确信息 ; accurate measurements｜精确测量 ; highly accurate｜高度精确的 ; an accurate prediction｜准确的预测
tip_zh: accurate强调准确无误；precise更强调细节精确。

meanings_zh: n. 自由 | n. 免受；摆脱
definition_en: the right to act freely | The state of not experiencing something unpleasant.
example1_en: Speech freedom is valued in many places.
example1_zh: 许多地方重视言论自由。
example2_en: Universities should protect academic freedom while encouraging researchers to consider the social consequences of their work.
example2_zh: 大学应保护学术自由，同时鼓励研究人员考虑其工作的社会影响。
collocations: freedom of speech｜言论自由 ; freedom to choose｜选择的自由 ; academic freedom｜学术自由 ; freedom from fear｜免于恐惧
tip_zh: freedom to do表示做某事的自由；from表示免受。

meanings_zh: adj. 基本的；根本的 | n. 基本原理；基础知识
definition_en: basic and important | A basic principle or skill, usually considered with others.
example1_en: Honesty is a fundamental value.
example1_zh: 诚实是基本价值观。
example2_en: Access to clean drinking water is a fundamental requirement for improving public health in disadvantaged communities.
example2_zh: 获得清洁饮用水是改善弱势社区公共卫生的基本条件。
collocations: fundamental to｜对……至关重要 ; a fundamental principle｜基本原则 ; fundamental change｜根本性改变 ; the fundamentals of｜……的基础知识
tip_zh: 名词通常用复数 fundamentals，表示基本原理。

meanings_zh: n. 事务；事件 | n. 婚外情；私情
definition_en: a matter or event | a romantic relationship involving someone committed to another partner
example1_en: Public affair need careful attention.
example1_zh: 公共事务需要认真关注。
example2_en: Schools can encourage young people to take an interest in current affairs through regular discussions of global events.
example2_zh: 学校可以通过定期讨论全球事件，鼓励年轻人关注时事。
collocations: current affairs｜时事 ; foreign affairs｜外交事务 ; a private affair｜私事 ; have an affair｜有婚外情
tip_zh: 表公共事务常用复数affairs，如current affairs。

meanings_zh: adj. 最初的 | n. 姓名首字母 | v. 用姓名首字母签署
definition_en: first | The first letter of a person's name | To mark a document with the first letters of your names
example1_en: My initial plan was wrong.
example1_zh: 我最初的计划是错的。
example2_en: Although the initial cost of solar panels is high, households may save money over the longer term.
example2_zh: 虽然太阳能电池板的初期费用较高，但从长远看，家庭可能节省开支。
collocations: initial reaction｜最初的反应 ; initial assessment｜初步评估 ; initial cost｜初期费用 ; initial stages｜初始阶段
tip_zh: 形容词通常放在名词前；姓名首字母常用initials。

meanings_zh: v. 宣布；声明 | v. 申报
definition_en: to state officially | to officially report goods, income or other required information
example1_en: The mayor will declare the festival open.
example1_zh: 市长将宣布节日开幕。
example2_en: Local authorities may declare a public holiday to encourage participation in an important community celebration.
example2_zh: 地方政府可能宣布放假一天，以鼓励民众参加重要的社区庆典。
collocations: declare a winner｜宣布获胜者 ; declare an emergency｜宣布进入紧急状态 ; declare goods｜申报物品 ; declare income｜申报收入
tip_zh: declare强调公开或正式宣布；海关申报也用此词。

definition_en: facts and figures
example1_en: Scientists collect data from tests.
example1_zh: 科学家从实验中收集数据。
example2_en: Reliable data allows policymakers to assess whether environmental regulations are reducing pollution in urban areas.
example2_zh: 可靠的数据能让政策制定者评估环境法规是否正在减少城市污染。
collocations: collect data｜收集数据 ; analyse data｜分析数据 ; personal data｜个人数据 ; data protection｜数据保护
tip_zh: 日常常作不可数名词；学术语境也用复数谓语。

meanings_zh: n. 环境；情况 | n. 经济状况；境遇
definition_en: a condition around an event | the conditions of someone's life, especially their financial situation
example1_en: Under no circumstance should you lie.
example1_zh: 在任何情况下你都不该说谎。
example2_en: Schools should consider each student's personal circumstances when developing policies on attendance and access to learning resources.
example2_zh: 学校制定出勤和学习资源获取政策时，应考虑每位学生的个人情况。
collocations: under the circumstances｜在这种情况下 ; personal circumstances｜个人情况 ; unforeseen circumstances｜意外情况 ; under no circumstances｜绝不
tip_zh: 常用复数；under no circumstances置句首须倒装。

meanings_zh: adj. 精致的；脆弱的 | adj. 微妙的；需谨慎处理的 | adj. 精巧的；柔和的
definition_en: fine; easily broken | Requiring careful handling to avoid problems or offence. | Fine, subtle, or gentle in appearance, flavour, or smell.
example1_en: Handle the glass with delicate care.
example1_zh: 轻拿轻放这些玻璃。
example2_en: Tourism in coastal regions must be carefully managed to protect delicate ecosystems from lasting damage.
example2_zh: 沿海地区的旅游业必须得到妥善管理，以保护脆弱的生态系统免遭长期破坏。
collocations: delicate balance｜微妙的平衡 ; delicate fabric｜易损面料 ; delicate flavour｜清淡的风味 ; delicate negotiations｜需谨慎进行的谈判
tip_zh: 既可形容易损物品，也可形容需谨慎处理的问题。

meanings_zh: v. 区分；辨别 | v. 成为…的特征；使有别于 | v. 看清；听出
definition_en: to tell apart | to make someone or something different from others | to see or hear something clearly enough to recognize it
example1_en: Babies learn to distinguish colors early.
example1_zh: 婴儿很早就能学会辨别颜色。
example2_en: Students should learn to distinguish reliable evidence from personal opinion when evaluating information online.
example2_zh: 学生在评估网络信息时，应学会区分可靠证据与个人观点。
collocations: distinguish between｜区分两者 ; distinguish A from B｜把A与B区分开 ; distinguish yourself｜使自己出众
tip_zh: 常用distinguish A from B或between A and B。

meanings_zh: adj. 灵活的 | adj. 柔韧的；易弯曲的
definition_en: able to change easily | able to bend easily without breaking
example1_en: Keep a flexible schedule.
example1_zh: 保持灵活的时间安排。
example2_en: Flexible working arrangements can help employees balance professional responsibilities with their family commitments.
example2_zh: 灵活的工作安排能帮助员工兼顾工作职责与家庭责任。
collocations: flexible working hours｜弹性工作时间 ; a flexible approach｜灵活的方法 ; flexible materials｜柔性材料
tip_zh: 既可形容安排灵活，也可形容材料易弯曲。

definition_en: a feeling of worry
example1_en: Exam anxiety is common among students.
example1_zh: 考试焦虑在学生中很常见。
example2_en: Regular physical activity can reduce anxiety among students facing demanding examinations and uncertain career prospects.
example2_zh: 经常锻炼可以减轻学生面对高难度考试和不确定就业前景时的焦虑。
collocations: anxiety about｜对……的焦虑 ; reduce anxiety｜减轻焦虑 ; severe anxiety｜严重焦虑
tip_zh: anxiety about后接担忧的事情；形容词是anxious。

meanings_zh: n. 冲突 | n. 矛盾；抵触 | v. 相冲突；相抵触
definition_en: a serious disagreement | A situation where different needs or ideas cannot agree. | To disagree with or be incompatible with something.
example1_en: Talking can reduce family conflict.
example1_zh: 沟通可以减少家庭冲突。
example2_en: Economic growth can conflict with environmental protection when industries rely heavily on fossil fuels.
example2_zh: 当工业高度依赖化石燃料时，经济增长可能与环境保护相冲突。
collocations: resolve a conflict｜解决冲突 ; conflict with｜与……相抵触 ; a conflict of interest｜利益冲突
tip_zh: 名词重音在首音节，动词重音在第二音节。

meanings_zh: v. 广播；播放 | n. 广播节目；播出
definition_en: to send out by radio or TV | A programme transmitted through radio, television, or the internet.
example1_en: The match will broadcast live tonight.
example1_zh: 比赛今晚将直播。
example2_en: Public television should broadcast educational programmes that help children understand science and develop an interest in learning.
example2_zh: 公共电视台应播出教育节目，帮助儿童理解科学并培养学习兴趣。
collocations: broadcast live｜现场直播 ; news broadcast｜新闻广播 ; broadcast a programme｜播出节目
tip_zh: 过去式和过去分词通常都为broadcast。

meanings_zh: n. 功能；作用 | v. 运转；发挥作用 | n. 函数
definition_en: the purpose of something | To work or operate in the intended way. | A mathematical relationship assigning each input exactly one output.
example1_en: What is the function of this button?
example1_zh: 这个按钮的功能是什么？
example2_en: Urban parks serve an important function by providing space for exercise, relaxation, and social interaction.
example2_zh: 城市公园提供运动、休闲和社交的空间，发挥着重要作用。
collocations: perform a function｜发挥作用 ; function properly｜正常运转 ; function as｜起……作用 ; basic function｜基本功能
tip_zh: function as后接名词，表示起……作用。

meanings_zh: n. 关心；担忧 | n. 令人担忧的事；关注事项 | v. 涉及；使担忧
definition_en: a worry or interest | An issue that matters or causes worry | To relate to someone or something, or cause worry
example1_en: Health is a shared concern for all.
example1_zh: 健康是所有人共同的关切。
example2_en: Growing concern about air pollution has encouraged many cities to invest in cleaner public transport systems.
example2_zh: 人们对空气污染日益担忧，促使许多城市投资建设更清洁的公共交通系统。
collocations: concern about safety｜对安全的担忧 ; raise concerns｜引发担忧 ; a major concern｜一个主要问题 ; concern for others｜对他人的关心
tip_zh: concern about多指对事情的担忧；for常指关心某人。

meanings_zh: n. 缺席；缺乏 | n. 缺乏；不存在
definition_en: the state of being away | a situation in which something does not exist or occur
example1_en: His absence from class worried the teacher.
example1_zh: 他缺课让老师担心。
example2_en: In the absence of reliable public transport, many residents have little choice but to drive.
example2_zh: 在缺乏可靠公共交通的情况下，许多居民别无选择，只能开车。
collocations: absence from work｜缺勤 ; in someone's absence｜在某人不在时 ; in the absence of｜在缺乏……的情况下 ; leave of absence｜获准休假
tip_zh: 缺席某活动用absence from；缺乏某物用absence of。

meanings_zh: adj. 持续的；不变的 | adj. 恒定的；不变的 | n. 常数；恒量
definition_en: happening all the time | remaining the same over time | a value or quantity that does not change
example1_en: There is constant noise from the street.
example1_zh: 街上有持续的噪音。
example2_en: Maintaining a constant temperature in public buildings can improve comfort but may increase energy consumption.
example2_zh: 公共建筑保持恒温可以提高舒适度，但可能增加能源消耗。
collocations: constant pressure｜持续的压力 ; constant temperature｜恒温 ; remain constant｜保持不变
tip_zh: 可指持续发生，也可指数值不变，须看语境。

meanings_zh: adj. 人造的；虚假的 | adj. 不自然的；做作的
definition_en: made by people, not natural | Not sincere or natural in appearance or behaviour
example1_en: artificial light can hurt sleep.
example1_zh: 人造光可能影响睡眠。
example2_en: Excessive artificial lighting in urban areas can disrupt wildlife behaviour and reduce the visibility of stars.
example2_zh: 城市中过量的人工照明会扰乱野生动物的行为，并使星星难以看清。
collocations: artificial intelligence｜人工智能 ; artificial lighting｜人工照明 ; artificial sweeteners｜人工甜味剂 ; an artificial smile｜做作的微笑
tip_zh: artificial指人造的；artistic才是艺术的。

meanings_zh: v. 分发；分配 | v. 使分布；使散布
definition_en: to give out | to spread something over an area
example1_en: Volunteers distribute food to the poor.
example1_zh: 志愿者向穷人分发食物。
example2_en: Governments must distribute healthcare resources fairly so that rural communities receive the same quality of care as urban residents.
example2_zh: 政府必须公平分配医疗资源，让农村社区享有与城市居民同等质量的医疗服务。
collocations: distribute food｜分发食物 ; distribute resources｜分配资源 ; evenly distributed｜均匀分布的 ; widely distributed｜广泛分布的
tip_zh: distribute A to B 表示“把A分发给B”。

meanings_zh: v. 贡献；捐献 | v. 促成；是原因之一 | v. 投稿；撰稿
definition_en: to give for a purpose | To help cause a particular result | To write material for a publication or website
example1_en: Everyone can contribute to the project.
example1_zh: 每个人都能为这个项目做贡献。
example2_en: Limited access to affordable housing can contribute to social inequality and force workers to accept longer commutes.
example2_zh: 难以获得可负担住房可能加剧社会不平等，并迫使劳动者接受更长的通勤时间。
collocations: contribute to a discussion｜参与讨论 ; contribute to economic growth｜促进经济增长 ; contribute funds｜捐助资金 ; contribute an article｜撰写稿件
tip_zh: contribute to中的to是介词，后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: adj. 绝对的；完全的 | adj. 绝对的；不受限制的
definition_en: total; complete | not limited by conditions, rules, or other authorities
example1_en: He has absolute confidence in the team.
example1_zh: 他对团队有绝对信心。
example2_en: Giving any single institution absolute power can weaken accountability and reduce public trust in government.
example2_zh: 赋予任何单一机构不受限制的权力，都可能削弱问责机制并降低公众对政府的信任。
collocations: absolute silence｜鸦雀无声 ; absolute certainty｜绝对肯定 ; absolute power｜绝对权力 ; an absolute necessity｜绝对必需的事物
tip_zh: 常表示程度已达极限，通常不用 very 修饰。

meanings_zh: v. 决定；测定 | v. 决定；影响结果 | v. 决定；下决心
definition_en: to decide firmly; to find out | To control or strongly influence what happens. | To make a firm decision to do something.
example1_en: Tests help determine your progress.
example1_zh: 测试有助于测定你的进步。
example2_en: Researchers must determine whether smaller classes improve learning outcomes before governments invest heavily in additional teaching staff.
example2_zh: 在政府投入大量资金增聘教师之前，研究人员必须确定小班教学是否能改善学习成果。
collocations: determine the cause｜查明原因 ; determine whether｜确定是否 ; determine the outcome｜决定结果 ; be determined to｜决心做……
tip_zh: determine whether 意为查明是否；后接从句。

meanings_zh: adj. 无辜的；天真的 | adj. 天真的；单纯的 | adj. 无恶意的；无害的
definition_en: not guilty; pure | Lacking experience or knowledge of unpleasant aspects of life. | Not intended to hurt, offend, or cause trouble.
example1_en: The child looked innocent.
example1_zh: 孩子看上去很天真。
example2_en: A fair legal system must protect innocent people while ensuring that those responsible for crimes face justice.
example2_zh: 公平的法律制度必须保护无辜者，同时确保犯罪者受到法律制裁。
collocations: innocent of a crime｜未犯某罪 ; innocent victims｜无辜的受害者 ; an innocent mistake｜无心之失
tip_zh: 表示未犯某罪用innocent of，不用innocent from。

meanings_zh: adj. 合适的 | v. 擅自占用；挪用 | v. 拨款；拨出
definition_en: suitable | to take something for your own use without permission | to officially set aside money for a particular purpose
example1_en: Wear appropriate clothes for the interview.
example1_zh: 面试穿合适的衣服。
example2_en: Governments should provide appropriate training to help workers adapt to technological changes in the labour market.
example2_zh: 政府应提供适当培训，帮助劳动者适应劳动力市场中的技术变革。
collocations: appropriate for｜适合于 ; appropriate measures｜适当措施 ; appropriate behaviour｜得体的行为 ; appropriate funds for｜为……拨款
tip_zh: 形容词词尾读/ət/，动词读/eɪt/。

meanings_zh: n. 便利 | n. 便利设施；方便的事物
definition_en: ease of use | Something that makes daily life easier.
example1_en: Online shopping offers great convenience.
example1_zh: 网购提供极大便利。
example2_en: Although online shopping offers convenience, it may encourage unnecessary spending and increase packaging waste.
example2_zh: 虽然网上购物带来了便利，但它可能助长不必要的消费，并增加包装垃圾。
collocations: for convenience｜为了方便 ; at your convenience｜在你方便时 ; modern conveniences｜现代便利设施 ; convenience store｜便利店
tip_zh: 表示“方便”通常不可数；形容词是convenient。

meanings_zh: n. 后果 | n. 重要性
definition_en: a result of an action | The quality of being important or worth considering.
example1_en: Every choice has a consequence.
example1_zh: 每个选择都有后果。
example2_en: One serious consequence of rapid urban growth is increased pressure on public transport and housing.
example2_zh: 城市快速扩张的一个严重后果是公共交通和住房承受的压力增大。
collocations: as a consequence｜因此 ; face the consequences｜面对后果 ; of little consequence｜无关紧要
tip_zh: as a consequence of后接原因，意为“由于”。

meanings_zh: v. 放弃；遗弃 | v. 放弃；终止 | n. 放纵；无拘无束
definition_en: to leave or give up | To stop doing or pursuing something before it is finished. | A lack of restraint in expressing feelings or enjoying yourself.
example1_en: We had to abandon the plan after the storm.
example1_zh: 暴风雨过后我们不得不放弃那个计划。
example2_en: Cities should not abandon ambitious recycling programmes simply because initial participation rates are lower than expected.
example2_zh: 城市不应仅因初期参与率低于预期，就放弃雄心勃勃的回收计划。
collocations: abandon a vehicle｜弃车 ; abandon a plan｜放弃计划 ; abandon hope｜放弃希望 ; with abandon｜纵情地
tip_zh: abandon直接接宾语；名词常见于with abandon。
